🌎 BEYOND THE 956

World-renowned conductor Herbert Blomstedt has died at 99.

Blomstedt died peacefully on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at his home in Gothenburg, Sweden, surrounded by family, his management confirmed. No cause of death was disclosed.

Born on July 11, 1927, in Springfield, Massachusetts, to Swedish parents, Blomstedt grew up in Gothenburg, where he attended symphony concerts twice a week as a young man. He began playing piano at six and violin at ten, and while studying at the Stockholm Royal College of Music he was chosen to conduct Brahms' Requiem — the moment his conducting career began.

His conducting debut came in 1954 with the Stockholm Philharmonic Orchestra, and that same year he became principal conductor of Sweden's Norrköping Symphony Orchestra. He went on to lead the Oslo Philharmonic, the Danish Radio Symphony, the Swedish Radio Symphony and the Staatskapelle Dresden, building a reputation especially for the music of German and Austrian composers.

From 1985 to 1995, Blomstedt was music director of the San Francisco Symphony, a decade widely credited with deepening the orchestra's sound and standing. He later served as music director of the Gewandhaus Orchestra in Leipzig, and remained conductor laureate of the San Francisco Symphony.

Across a career spanning seven decades, Blomstedt continued to conduct into his late 90s. He gave his final performance in May 2026, at age 98, with the San Francisco Symphony. His manager of almost 40 years, Lothar Schacke, said: "Each encounter with him was a gift, his kindness, knowledge, wisdom, and gentle humour enriching us intellectually and emotionally."

Rest in Peace, Herbert Blomstedt.

Sources: Classic FM, reporting his management's confirmation; The Guardian; The New York Times.
